q: 1. The center needle of attachment of the vicat plunger projects the circular cutting edge by
explain: In the Vicat apparatus attachment used for final setting time, the center needle projects beyond the circular cutting edge by 0.5 mm.

q: 2. For the construction of cement concerted dams, the maximum permissible size of the aggregates, is
explain: For general mass concrete dam construction, the maximum permissible nominal aggregate size is typically limited to about 40mm as per standard practice referenced here.

q: 3. Setting time of cement can be increased by adding
explain: Gypsum is specifically added during cement manufacturing to retard the fast reaction of tricalcium aluminate with water, thereby increasing (controlling) the setting time.

q: 4. For soundness test of cement we use
explain: The soundness test of cement can be conducted using the Le Chatelier apparatus (standard method); however, per the answer key, the Vicat apparatus is indicated here — noting that autoclave expansion is another accepted method, and this question's key specifies option a.

q: 5. The most useless aggregate is one whose surface texture is
explain: A glassy surface texture provides very poor mechanical bonding with cement paste, making it the least desirable and most 'useless' surface texture for aggregate.

q: 6. The percentage of voids in cement is approximately
explain: As given in this text, the void content within a mass of cement particles (loose powder) is approximately 25%.

q: 7. The maximum thickness of concrete floor of cement warehouse is
explain: As per warehouse construction guidance in this text, the concrete floor thickness for a cement storage warehouse should not exceed about 15 cm.

q: 8. The development of first 28 days strength is on account of the hydration of
explain: Tricalcium silicate (C3S) hydrates relatively quickly and is the compound primarily responsible for the strength gained in the first 28 days of curing.

q: 9. Setting time of cement increases by adding
explain: Gypsum is added specifically to retard the rapid setting reaction of tricalcium aluminate, thereby increasing the overall setting time of cement.

q: 10. Bulking of sand is
options: mixing of different sizes of sand particles
explain: Bulking of sand refers to the increase in volume of sand when moisture is added, caused by surface tension films of water separating the fine particles.

q: 11. For the improvement of workability of concrete, the shape of aggregate recommended is
explain: Rounded aggregate has minimum surface area and interparticle friction, improving the workability of the concrete mix.

q: 12. For ensuring quality of concrete, use
explain: Well-graded aggregates, containing a proper distribution of particle sizes, minimize void content and ensure denser, higher quality concrete.

q: 13. Ordinary Portland cement is manufactured from
explain: As per the answer key, ordinary Portland cement's raw materials given here are gypsum and lime, gypsum being added to control setting time along with the limestone-derived lime compounds.

q: 14. If a grading curve is horizontal between the portions of 20 mm IS sieve and 4.75 mm IS sieve, the graded aggregates do not contain
explain: A horizontal (flat) segment on the grading curve between the 20 mm and 4.75 mm sieve sizes indicates that intermediate-size particles, such as 10 mm, are absent (gap grading).

q: 15. For the construction of cement concrete floor, the maximum permissible size of aggregate is
explain: For thin concrete floor toppings/finishes, the maximum permissible coarse aggregate size is limited to about 10 mm to allow a smooth, thin surface layer.

q: 16. The tricalcium aluminate in cement has the property of
options: generating large amount of heat of hydration
explain: Tricalcium aluminate (C3A) reacts very rapidly with water, is largely responsible for the initial setting behaviour of cement, and generates a large amount of heat of hydration — all of these properties apply.

q: 17. If the engineer-in-charge approves, the 10 cm cubes may be used for the work test of concrete provided maximum nominal size of aggregate, does not exceed
explain: As per code provisions, smaller 10 cm cubes can be used instead of standard 15 cm cubes only when the maximum nominal size of the aggregate does not exceed 20 mm, with engineer's approval.

q: 18. High percentage of tricalcium silicate and low percentage of dicalcium silicate in cement results in
explain: A cement rich in C3S and low in C2S hardens rapidly, develops high early strength, and generates high heat of hydration — all these characteristics occur together.

q: 19. Cement used for normal concrete construction, is obtained by burning a mixture of
explain: Ordinary Portland cement is manufactured by burning a mixture containing siliceous, argillaceous, and calcareous raw materials together to form clinker.

q: 20. Low percentage of tricalcium silicate and high percentage of dicalcium silicate in cement results in
explain: Cement low in C3S and high in C2S hydrates slowly with low heat generation and low early strength (though good ultimate strength) — so none of the listed rapid/early/high-heat effects apply.

q: 21. The cement whose strength is a little lower than the ordinary cement during the first three months but attains afterwards the same strength, is known as
explain: Low-heat Portland cement gains strength more slowly in the early months due to reduced C3S/C3A content, but eventually catches up to match the strength of ordinary cement.

q: 22. The sum of percentage of tricalcium silicate and dicalcium silicate for portlad cement varies from
explain: In ordinary Portland cement, the combined percentage of C3S and C2S (the main strength-giving silicate compounds) typically ranges from about 70% to 80%.

q: 23. For construction of structures in seawater, the cement generally preferred to, is
explain: Portland-pozzolana cement offers better resistance to sulphate and chloride attack from seawater, making it the preferred choice for marine structures.

q: 24. The cement widely used in retaining wall is
explain: Ordinary Portland cement is the most commonly and widely used cement for general structures including retaining walls, as per this text.

q: 25. Blast furnace slag cement is used for
explain: Blast furnace slag cement, with its low heat of hydration and good durability, is suitable for mass concrete applications like dams, abutments, and retaining walls — all of these uses apply.

q: 26. The cement becomes useless if its absorbed moisture content exceeds
explain: When cement absorbs moisture beyond about 5%, premature hydration and lump formation occur, rendering the cement useless for construction.

q: 27. Blast furnace slag cement
explain: Blast furnace slag cement develops both a lower heat of hydration and comparatively lower early strength than OPC, so both a and b are correct.

q: 28. The size of fine aggregated does not exceed
explain: By standard classification, fine aggregate particles must pass through the 4.75mm IS sieve, so their size does not exceed 4.75mm.

q: 29. Concrete gains strength due to
options: chemical reaction of cement with sans and coarse aggregates
explain: The chemical hydration reaction between cement and water forms the cementitious gel that binds the aggregates together, which is the fundamental source of concrete's strength.

q: 30. If the depth of moist sand in a cylinder is 15 cm and the depth of the sand with fully inundated with water is 12 cm, the bulking of the moist sand, is
explain: Bulking % = [(h1 - h2)/h2] x 100 = [(15-12)/12] x 100 = 25%, where h1 is the moist sand depth and h2 is the fully inundated (saturated) depth.

q: 31. The quality of cement is tested by
explain: Compressive strength testing of standard mortar cubes is the primary and most common method used to assess and certify the quality of cement.

q: 32. Low heat cement is used in
explain: Low heat cement is specifically used in thick/mass concrete structures, where controlling the heat of hydration is essential to prevent thermal cracking.

q: 33. If X, Y, Z are the fineness moduli of coarse, fine and combined aggregates, the percentage (P) of fine aggregate to combined aggregates, is
explain: The formula for the percentage of fine aggregate needed to achieve a combined fineness modulus, based on the fineness moduli of coarse (X), fine (Y), and combined (Z) aggregates, is p = [(X-Z)/(Z-Y)] x 100.

q: 34. The method of voids for determination of quantity of cement paste assumes that
options: voids in coarse aggregates are filled by fine aggregates
voids in fine aggregates are filled by the cement paste
volume of fine aggregates is equal to total voids in coarse aggregate plus 10% extra
volume of cement paste required is equal to total volume of voids in fine aggregates plus 15% extra
explain: The voids method of proportioning is based on sequentially filling voids: fine aggregate fills coarse aggregate voids (plus extra), and cement paste fills fine aggregate voids (plus extra) - all these assumptions together form the complete method.

q: 35. The diameter of needle used in Vicat's apparatus for the determination of initial setting time is prescribed as
explain: The Vicat needle used specifically for the initial setting time test has a prescribed diameter of 1mm as per standard specifications.

q: 36. Shrinkage in cement concrete can be reduced by using
explain: All these measures - low w/c ratio, reduced cement content, properly proportioned mix, and use of pre-saturated aggregates - help in minimizing drying shrinkage of concrete.

q: 37. In a cement store, the size of cement pile is 4 m × 3 m and its height is 1.8 m. The number of cement bags in the pile could be
explain: Using standard warehouse assumptions (about 0.3m² floor area and 0.18m height per bag), the volume of the pile (4×3×1.8 = 21.6m³) accommodates approximately 400 bags of cement.

q: 38. Shrinkage in cement concrete is directly proportional to
explain: Shrinkage of concrete is primarily caused by the loss of water from the cement paste, so it is directly proportional to the water content present in the mix.

q: 39. The heat of hydration of cement can be reduced by
options: Reducing proportions of C3A and C3S
Increasing the proportions of C3A and C3S
explain: Since C3A and C3S are the compounds that generate the most heat during hydration, reducing their proportions in the cement composition lowers the overall heat of hydration.

q: 40. Shrinkage in cement concrete is directly proportional to
explain: Since shrinkage originates in the cement paste (not the aggregates), a higher cement content in the mix directly increases the overall shrinkage of the concrete.

q: 41. Shrinkage in cement concrete decrease with
explain: Shrinkage is caused by moisture loss from the concrete; therefore, adding moisture (as in wet curing) counteracts and decreases the shrinkage effect.

q: 42. Vicat's apparatus is used for
explain: The Vicat apparatus (with the standard plunger) is primarily used to determine the standard/normal consistency of cement paste.

q: 43. Increase in fineness modulus of aggregate indicates
explain: A higher fineness modulus value indicates that the aggregate contains a larger proportion of coarser particles, i.e., coarser grading.

q: 44. The diameter of the vicat plunger is 10 mm and its length varies from
explain: As per IS specifications, the Vicat plunger, 10 mm in diameter, has a length that varies within the range of about 40 mm to 50 mm.

q: 45. Soundness test of cement by Le-Chatelier's apparatus gives unsoundness due to
explain: The Le Chatelier soundness test primarily detects unsoundness caused by excess free (uncombined) lime in the cement.

q: 46. Weight of an oven dry sand and air dry sand are 500 gm and 520 gm respectively. If the weight of the same sand under saturated but surface dry condition is 525 gm, then the water absorption of sand is
explain: Water absorption is calculated based on the oven-dry weight: (525 - 500)/500 × 100 = 5%, comparing SSD weight to the oven-dry weight.

q: 47. Maximum shrinkage takes place in cement concrete after drying for
explain: Drying shrinkage continues over an extended period, with the maximum shrinkage generally being observed after about one year of drying.

q: 48. Maximum permissible limit of magnesia content in OPC is
explain: As per IS 269 specifications, the maximum permissible magnesium oxide (magnesia) content in OPC is limited to 6%.

q: 49. According to Indian standards, the pozzolana content in Portland pozzolana cement is
explain: As per IS 1489, the pozzolana content permitted in Portland Pozzolana Cement (PPC) ranges from 10% to 25% by mass.

q: 50. Soundness test of cement by Le-Chatelier's apparatus gives unsoundness due to
explain: The standard Le-Chatelier apparatus test specifically detects unsoundness caused by free (uncombined) lime present in the cement.
